criteria.description: Local elevation range (max - min within AOI) representing basin vs. crater-rim topography.
Mean terrain slope (degrees) derived from DEM; critical for rover mobility and landing safety.
Mean / seasonal minimum surface temperature proxy (with explicit planetary atmosphere caveats).
Atmospheric water limitation proxy (1 - P/PET). Marked non-comparable for airless Lunar targets.
Jaccard + abundance overlap of dominant mineral groups (clays, sulfates, chlorides, basalts, oxides).
Soluble salts, perchlorates/chlorides, pH, and redox chemistry from in-situ or rover measurements.

planetary_aois.name: Jezero Crater — Western Delta & Margin
planetary_aois.summary: Ancient paleolake basin and river delta investigated by NASA Perseverance; hosts Mg-carbonates, Fe/Mg smectites, sulfates, and evaporitic salts.

planetary_aois.name: Oxia Planum — Clay-Bearing Plain
planetary_aois.summary: ESA ExoMars Rosalind Franklin landing site; extensive Fe/Mg smectite-vermiculite and hydrated silica plains formed by ancient aqueous alteration.

planetary_aois.name: Gale Crater — Mount Sharp Sulfate Unit
planetary_aois.summary: Curiosity rover field site transitioning from ancient lacustrine mudstones to sulfate-bearing and chloride-rich evaporitic strata.

planetary_aois.name: Shackleton Crater Rim — South Pole Base AOI
planetary_aois.summary: High-illumination ridge bordering a Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) with potential water-ice traps; primary candidate for a permanent Moon base.

planetary_aois.name: Mare Tranquillitatis — Basalt Pit & Regolith
planetary_aois.summary: High-titanium mare basalt plain featuring skylight pits linked to subsurface lava tubes, offering natural radiation and thermal shielding.

earth_sites.name: Tindouf Basin — Sebkha & Evaporite Margin
earth_sites.summary: Hyperarid Saharan evaporite basin with documented soluble salt assemblages (chlorides, sulfates, nitrates, and perchlorate analogs) analogous to Martian evaporitic soils.

publications.citation: Oberlin, E. A., Claire, M. W., & Kounaves, S. P. (2018). Evaluation of the Tindouf Basin as a Mars Analog for Soluble Salt Geochemistry. Astrobiology.
publications.key_finding: Demonstrates high concentrations of soluble chlorides and sulfates in hyperarid evaporitic crusts relevant to Mars Phoenix and Gale soil chemistry.

limits: Earth atmospheric pressure (~1 bar) and daytime temperatures (+25°C to +45°C) differ sharply from Martian cryogenic surface conditions.
Logistics and cross-border access require regional field permits.
earth_sites.position_reference: Barycentre de la Sebkha de Tindouf / station Oberlin 2018
earth_sites.position_source: Oberlin et al., 2018 (GPS terrain); Copernicus GLO-30
earth_sites.sector_note: Secteur d'évaporites et de croûtes salines hyperarides documenté par spectroscopie SWIR et diffraction RX.

earth_sites.name: Lake Iriqui — Sebkha & Paléolac (Southern Morocco)
earth_sites.summary: Accessible Moroccan paleolake playa and braided wadi fan system with evaporite crusts, clay flats, and low-slope rover test corridors.

publications.citation: Ori, G. G. et al. — Draa / Anti-Atlas Mars Analog Field Campaigns (Morocco Planetary Analog Testbed).
publications.key_finding: Fluvial-lacustrine fan morphology and evaporitic playa flats provide safe, accessible testbeds for rover navigation and stratigraphy.

limits: Seasonal ephemeral flooding can briefly alter surface salt crust state.
Soluble perchlorate/salt assay is missing in current harmonized database — relies on orbital SWIR mineralogy only.
earth_sites.position_reference: Barycentre du paléolac asséché d'Iriqui (Playa centrale)
earth_sites.sector_note: Secteur paléolac à fond plat et argiles évaporitiques (parfait pour essais de mobilité basse pente et stratigraphie).

earth_sites.name: Atacama Desert — Yungay Hyperarid Core
earth_sites.summary: World's driest non-polar desert; benchmark for extreme water-limitation, natural perchlorate/nitrate soils, and trace organic biosignature preservation.

publications.citation: Navarro-González, R. et al. (2003). Mars-Like Soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the Dry Limit of Microbial Life. Science, 302(5647).
publications.key_finding: Yungay soils show ultra-low microbial biomass and strong oxidizing chemistry analogous to Viking Mars soil experiments.

limits: Mean surface temperature (~16°C) is much warmer than Mars or Lunar South Pole.
Nitrate enrichment in Atacama exceeds known Martian abundances.

geochemistry.provenance: Navarro-González et al. (2003) + Catling et al.

earth_sites.position_reference: Station d'échantillonnage biologique Yungay Core (Bassin d'Aguas Blancas)
earth_sites.sector_note: Secteur hyperaride d'Aguas Blancas avec grille altimétrique haute résolution Copernicus DEM.

earth_sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (University Valley)
earth_sites.summary: Cold, hyperarid polar desert with ice-cemented permafrost, sublimation polygons, and cryogenic thermal regimes analogous to high-latitude Mars and polar Moon operations.

publications.citation: Doran, P. T. et al. (2002) & Tamppari, L. K. et al. — McMurdo Dry Valleys as a Terrestrial Analog for Mars Cryosphere & Polar Permafrost.
publications.key_finding: Sublimation-controlled permafrost and sub-zero hyperaridity closely replicate Mars Phoenix and high-latitude ice stability.

limits: Extremely high logistical cost, strict Antarctic Treaty environmental protocols, and short seasonal access window.
Lacks abundant Mg/Fe phyllosilicates compared to Oxia Planum or Jezero.

geochemistry.provenance: Kounaves et al. Antarctic perchlorate assays

earth_sites.position_reference: Station permafrost University Valley (Beacon Valley ridge)
earth_sites.position_source: Doran et al., 2002; REMA / USGS LTER
earth_sites.sector_note: Score régional · emprise de calcul non documentée (caractérisation stationnaire LTER).

earth_sites.name: Haughton Impact Structure (Devon Island)
earth_sites.summary: 23-km impact crater in a polar desert with impact breccia, gullies, ground ice, and decades of NASA/CSA Mars & Lunar rover traverse testing.

publications.citation: Lee, P. & Osinski, G. R. (2005). The Haughton-Mars Project: Overview of Science Investigations at the Haughton Impact Structure.
publications.key_finding: Preserved impact breccia and crater rim slopes provide high-fidelity terrain for both Mars craters and Lunar South Pole rover traverses.

limits: Carbonate-rich target rocks differ from Martian basaltic crust.
Only accessible during brief Arctic summer windows.
earth_sites.position_reference: Camp de base HMP / bordure centrale du cratère d'impact
earth_sites.sector_note: Score régional · emprise de calcul non documentée (synthèse de traverses rover).

earth_sites.name: Río Tinto — Acidic Sulfate Basin
earth_sites.summary: Extremely acidic iron- and sulfate-rich river basin (jarosite, hematite, goethite) serving as a premier mineralogical analog for Gale and Meridiani Planum.

publications.citation: Fernández-Remolar, D. C. et al. (2005). The Río Tinto Basin, Spain: Mineralogy, sedimentary geobiology, and implications for interpretation of outcrop rocks at Meridiani Planum, Mars.
publications.key_finding: Jarosite and ferric sulfate precipitates match Opportunity and Curiosity orbital/in-situ detections.

limits: Humid Mediterranean climate and active surface liquid water make it a poor climatic/aridity analog.
Anthropogenic mining overprint must be separated from natural gossan formations.
earth_sites.position_reference: Affleurement gossan minéralogique Peña de Hierro
earth_sites.sector_note: Score régional · emprise de calcul non documentée (mesures ponctuelles de cours d'eau acide).

earth_sites.name: Lanzarote — Corona Lava Tubes & Basaltic Plains
earth_sites.status: Lunar & Mars Rover / Lava Tube Analog
earth_sites.summary: Unweathered basaltic lava flows, pyroclastic regolith, and accessible lava tubes used by ESA PANGAEA astronaut and rover training.

publications.citation: Sauro, F. et al. (2019). ESA PANGAEA: Planetary Analog Geological Training in Lanzarote Volcanic Terrains & Lava Tubes.
publications.key_finding: Basaltic lava tubes and rough scoria fields replicate Lunar Mare Tranquillitatis pits and Martian volcanic rover hazards.

limits: Oceanic island humidity and mild temperatures do not match Mars or Lunar thermal extremes.
Lacks significant evaporitic soluble salt crusts.
earth_sites.position_reference: Tube de lave Cueva de los Verdes / terrain d'entraînement ESA PANGAEA
earth_sites.position_source: Sauro et al., 2019; Cabildo de Lanzarote LiDAR
earth_sites.sector_note: Score régional · emprise de calcul non documentée (couloir de tube volcanique).

earth_sites.name: Mojave Desert — Silver Lake & Dumont Dunes
earth_sites.summary: Classic NASA JPL rover engineering testbed combining alluvial fans, desert pavements, evaporitic playa flats, and steep dune/ridge slopes.

publications.citation: Arvidson, R. E. et al. — Mojave Desert Rover Mobility & Spectral Testbed Investigations (JPL / NASA).
publications.key_finding: Provides rapid logistical access and controlled alluvial/playa slope gradients for rover slip and wheel-wear validation.

limits: Semi-arid to arid climate with higher organic carbon background than hyperarid Atacama or Tindouf.
In-situ trace perchlorate assay not harmonized in this catalog slice.
earth_sites.position_reference: Playa de Silver Lake / corridor de test rover JPL
earth_sites.position_source: USGS 3DEP DEM / JPL Rover Field Tests
earth_sites.sector_note: Score régional · emprise de calcul non documentée (synthèse régionale de dunes et playas).

earth_sites.name: Vallée du Drâa — Cône Alluvial & Chenaux Tressés (Morocco)
earth_sites.summary: Braided fluvial fan system and low-slope alluvial gravel plains in the Moroccan Anti-Atlas, benchmarked for ExoMars rover mobility trials.
earth_sites.position_reference: Terrasse alluviale de Tagounite / cône fluviatile du Drâa
earth_sites.position_source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 / Ori et al., 2014
earth_sites.sector_note: Secteur de cône alluvial et terrasses de cailloutis modélisé par grille Copernicus DEM 30m.

publications.citation: Ori, G. G. et al. — Draa Mars Analog Field Campaigns (Morocco Planetary Analog Testbed).
publications.key_finding: Fluvial fan gravels and terrace topography provide an ideal physical test corridor for planetary rover chassis and autonomous traverse algorithms.

limits: Minimal clay and perchlorate deposits compared to Tindouf Sebkha evaporites.
Vegetation pockets in oued margins require exclusion filters.
